regulatory.what: Two new EU AI Act prohibitions apply: systems that generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery. Machine-readable marking of synthetic output under Article 50(2) also applies to generative systems already on the market
regulatory.who: Any firm offering generative AI in the EU
regulatory.todo: Confirm your vendors mark synthetic output and that your own builds do too
regulatory.title: EU AI Act: new prohibitions and synthetic-content marking apply

regulatory.what: FINRA's 2027 oversight report, if it follows the 2026 report's release on 9 December 2025
regulatory.todo: Re-read the 2026 report's agent section and check you can track agent actions and decisions
regulatory.title: FINRA 2027 oversight report expected

regulatory.what: Colorado's Automated Decision-Making Technology in Consequential Decisions Act takes effect, replacing the 2024 Colorado AI Act: notice before use, an explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome, and meaningful human review on request
regulatory.who: Developers and deployers using automated decisions in lending, insurance, employment and other covered areas for Colorado consumers
regulatory.todo: Identify which automated decisions reach Colorado consumers; deployers keep compliance records for three years after each use
regulatory.title: Colorado automated decision-making law takes effect

regulatory.what: The FCA publishes its evaluation of the second AI Live Testing cohort: Aereve, Barclays, Coadjute, Experian, GoCardless, Lloyds Banking Group (Scottish Widows), Palindrome and UBS. Testing ends by the end of 2026
regulatory.todo: Read it for the supervisor's view of production AI in banking, payments and credit data
regulatory.title: FCA evaluation of the second AI Live Testing cohort

regulatory.what: The US banking agencies' request for information on model risk and "banks' use of AI, including generative AI and agentic AI", promised in April when SR 26-2 left both out of scope. Not in the Federal Register as of 24 October 2026
regulatory.todo: Prepare your answer now: how you validate retrieval, guardrails and agent actions, and how you would stop an agent
regulatory.title: US bank regulators' request for information on AI

regulatory.what: A ruling on OpenAI's and Microsoft's summary judgment motions in the news publishers' copyright cases, including New York Times v. OpenAI. The publishers filed their opposition in October 2026; no ruling date has been set
regulatory.who: Anyone training or fine-tuning on third-party content
regulatory.todo: Inventory the provenance of every corpus your models touch
regulatory.title: Ruling on summary judgment in the publishers' copyright cases against OpenAI and Microsoft

regulatory.what: The first lawsuit brought in the name of the DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, created under the executive order of 11 December 2025. The DOJ intervened on 24 April 2026 in xAI's challenge to the 2024 Colorado AI Act, which Colorado then repealed and replaced
regulatory.who: Firms planning around state AI laws
regulatory.todo: Avoid building compliance around any single state regime until this settles
regulatory.title: First DOJ AI Litigation Task Force lawsuit

regulatory.what: General-purpose AI models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 must comply; each member state must have at least one operational AI regulatory sandbox
regulatory.who: Model providers directly; firms that fine-tune or rebrand models
regulatory.todo: Ask your model vendors for their compliance position and documentation
regulatory.title: EU AI Act: legacy general-purpose AI models must comply

regulatory.what: EU AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply, including creditworthiness and credit scoring of individuals, life and health insurance pricing, and recruitment
regulatory.who: Lenders, insurers and employers using AI in the EU
regulatory.todo: Start conformity and logging work now; deployers must keep logs for at least six months
regulatory.title: EU AI Act: high-risk obligations for Annex III systems

regulatory.what: High-risk obligations for AI built into products regulated under Annex I apply
regulatory.todo: Note it; little action for most financial firms
regulatory.title: EU AI Act: high-risk obligations for Annex I products

news.headline: Law firms read the OCC's new AI examiner framework
news.why: Outside counsel are already telling banks what examiners will ask for. Expect the questions to land on vendors before they land on policy.

news.headline: Zapier surveys 513 US leaders on AI agents
news.why: A vendor survey, so read it as direction rather than proof. It is useful for the gap between agents planned and agents running in production.

news.headline: Edelman and LinkedIn on what executives do with thought leadership
news.why: The measure that matters is what a reader does next, not whether they read. That is the bar for every piece we publish.

news.headline: OCC publishes Bulletin 2026-54, an examiner framework for bank AI
news.why: It is examiner guidance and sets no new expectations for banks on its own. It still tells you which records an exam will ask to see.

news.headline: CMI and MarketingProfs publish the 2026 B2B content trends
news.why: A survey of 1,132 marketers, mostly in North America. Read it for where budgets are moving, not for what works.

news.headline: Menlo Ventures publishes its 2026 State of Enterprise AI
news.why: Nearly 400 enterprise buyers on where AI spend is going. Menlo invests in AI companies, so weigh it against buyer-side data.

news.headline: Ahrefs measures how stable AI citations are
news.why: About 37,500 citations tracked over 20 days. Being cited once is not the same as being cited next week, so track it.

news.headline: AICPA proposes updated SOC 2 trust services criteria
news.why: An exposure draft, so the criteria can still change. AI vendors in security review should know it is coming.

news.headline: First harmonised standard published under the EU AI Act
news.why: EN 18286 turns parts of the Act into something an auditor can check. Firms working towards ISO 42001 should map the overlap.

news.headline: US bank regulators ask whether lenders can stop their AI agents
news.why: The question is shifting from whether a model is accurate to whether someone can halt it. The kill switch is becoming a control.

news.headline: Meta reports third-quarter 2026 results
news.why: Price per ad reflects performance and mix as well as competition. Read the change carefully before blaming the auction.

news.headline: Google to require licence proof from US and Canadian financial advertisers in 2027
news.why: Exact dates and scope are not yet published. Fintechs that rely on paid search should start gathering licence evidence now.

news.headline: European Commission updates its AI literacy questions and answers
news.why: Official guidance, not law, but it sets the date supervision starts. An acceptable use policy plus training records is the practical answer.

news.headline: FCA sets out good and poor practice for AI in financial services
news.why: Examples only, with no new rules. It is still the clearest public list of what the UK regulator wants to see.

news.headline: Q3 2026 venture data: billion-dollar rounds mask a narrowing market
news.why: Headline totals are carried by a few very large rounds. Most companies are raising in a tighter market than the totals suggest.

news.headline: Bloomberg launches Enterprise MCP for AI data access
news.why: Licensed market data is now reachable by agents through a standard connector. Check the licence before you check the latency.

news.headline: Reuters: banking watchdogs step up AI scrutiny
news.why: Based on unnamed sources, so treat it as a signal. It fits the run of examiner guidance that followed in November.

news.headline: Google folds enterprise AI into a single Gemini agent
news.why: Suite vendors are bundling memory and context into the agent. The open question is whether your decisions stay readable outside it.

news.headline: AWS on access control for retrieval with Amazon Quick and Bedrock
news.why: Vendor-written, but a useful pattern: the retriever should only see what the person asking is allowed to see.

news.headline: The CLARITY Act stalls in the Senate
news.why: US market structure stays unsettled into 2027. Token decisions should work without counting on it passing.

news.headline: WFA study: global brands move away from paying agencies for time
news.why: Fees tied to outputs and outcomes are replacing hours. Ask any agency what the fee is tied to before you sign.

news.headline: IAB Tech Lab finalises podcast measurement v2.3, now covering video
news.why: Video podcasts finally have a shared counting rule. Ask sponsors which version their numbers follow.

news.headline: KPMG Q3 2026 AI Pulse survey
news.why: Large-company leaders on agent deployment. Useful as a benchmark for how far peers have actually got.

news.headline: BLS publishes Employee Tenure in 2026
news.why: People move on faster than decisions expire. That is the case for writing down why, not just what.

news.headline: IAB Europe: agentic ad buying gains ground
news.why: An industry survey summary without a stated sample size. A signal of direction for publishers, not a measure.
